headline: Google Quantum AI solves molecular benchmarks in under 5 minutes on 105-qubit Willow chip
summary: Google's 105-qubit Willow processor executed complex molecular chemistry calculations in 282 seconds. This task would require approximately 4,200 years on the world's fastest classical exascale supercomputer.
details: Google Quantum AI has unveiled rigorous empirical benchmarks proving verifiable quantum computational advantage on its new 105-qubit Willow processor. It executed ground-state electronic structure calculations for industrial transition-metal complexes in 282 seconds.

This workload was verified to require approximately 4,200 years of continuous processing on the world's fastest classical exascale supercomputer, Frontier. Unlike earlier demonstrations, Willow targets real-world molecular chemistry Hamiltonians.

The 105-qubit array utilizes a planar square grid of superconducting transmon qubits with tunable capacitive couplers. Willow achieves a two-qubit gate fidelity of 99.84% and single-qubit gate error of 0.038%.

Crucially, Willow crosses the theoretical error-correction threshold, enabling engineers to implement dynamic distance-5 and distance-7 surface code patches. These actively diagnose and correct physical bit-flip and phase-flip faults in real time.

The benchmark simulation centered on determining the active-site catalytic mechanism of nitrogenase iron-molybdenum cofactor (FeMoco), critical to biological nitrogen fixation. Classical quantum chemistry methods suffer from exponential scaling walls when tracking strongly correlated electron entanglement.

Willow executed an optimized Phase Estimation and Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) algorithm combined with zero-noise extrapolation error mitigation. It evaluated 54 active molecular orbitals across 108 spin-orbitals simultaneously.

The entire computation converged to chemical accuracy within 4 minutes and 42 seconds, establishing an absolute verification point. Google states Willow is solving concrete, non-trivial Hamiltonian equations that directly inform catalytic chemistry and battery material discovery.

For the first time, quantum hardware is demonstrating utility that classical silicon clusters cannot economically match. Early access allocations are opening for select pharmaceutical partners and semiconductor research consortia under the Google Quantum Cloud umbrella.

Researchers will utilize Willow to explore room-temperature superconductor candidates, synthetic fertilizer synthesis pathways, and cathode degradation kinetics for next-generation solid-state lithium batteries. This confirms that intermediate quantum architectures have arrived at commercial industrial relevance.

headline_marked: [[Meta releases Llama 4 Scout]] with native 1M-token context and Mixture-of-Depths architecture
headline: Meta releases Llama 4 Scout with native 1M-token context and Mixture-of-Depths architecture
summary: This open-source model features a dynamic Mixture-of-Depths architecture, achieving parity with leading closed-source AI on benchmarks while running efficiently on dual-GPU workstations.
details: Meta's FAIR team has officially released Llama 4 Scout, the first frontier-class open-source foundation model built natively on dynamic Mixture-of-Depths (MoD) routing. It boasts a total parameter capacity of 105 billion, with only 24 billion active parameters per token, and a native 1,000,000-token context window.

Unlike standard dense transformers that allocate identical compute to every token, Llama 4 Scout uses a learned top-k routing gate in each block. This dynamically assigns computation based on token complexity, allowing simple tokens to bypass deep layers while complex ones receive maximal processing.

This dynamic depth allocation reduces generation latency by 58% compared to dense 70B models, while expanding overall model capacity. It supports a native 1M-token context window with zero degradation, utilizing RingAttention and sliding-window multi-head latent attention.

Previous open-weights models often relied on post-training RoPE interpolation for long contexts, leading to performance issues beyond 64K tokens. Llama 4 Scout was trained from scratch with an 8-stage progressive context expansion curriculum up to 1,048,576 tokens.

On the industry-standard Needle In A Haystack (NIAH) benchmark, Llama 4 Scout achieved 99.8% retrieval accuracy across the entire 1M token spectrum. The model can effortlessly process multi-volume legal documents, full-stack software repositories, and extensive scientific literature in a single prompt.

Independent third-party audits show Llama 4 Scout resolved 48.6% of real-world GitHub issues autonomously on SWE-bench Verified. This places it within striking distance of proprietary commercial leaders, offering full self-hosting freedom.

Checkpoints for base, instruction-tuned, and quantized variants (including FP8 and INT4 AWQ) are now available on Hugging Face and Meta's official portal. It requires just 24GB VRAM in 4-bit mode, capable of running on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090/5090.

Native runtime support has already been merged into vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, and Hugging Face TGI. This enables developers to deploy self-hosted instances across enterprise Kubernetes clusters immediately, providing frontier-level capabilities without per-token API charges.
